(a) operational failures that provoke high financial and legal liability risk are more likely to spur problem-solving activities than other failures, and (b) management communication and engagement with frontline workers can encourage problem solving.

(a) problem solving is especially likely following reported incidents that provoke financial and/or legal liability risks, and (b) problem solving is also more likely to follow reported incidents when managers communicate and engage with frontline workers.
problem solving is most likely to occur after operational failures that are likely to lead to financial or legal liability risks.

the conditions under which reported operational failures will be used as a source of knowledge for problem solving.
the conditions that encourage problem solving following the identification of operational failures.

our study shows that the problem solving process can be stimulated by the reporting of operational failures that provoke liability risks and by management commitment to problem-solving.

the problem solving process is more likely to be initiated when the problems have financial or legal consequences and that the problem solving activities are more likely to occur when managers engage in communication and problem solving activities.

problem solving is more likely to follow reported incidents that provoke liability risks and that management practices can influence the likelihood of problem solving.
